reason: The doc-history row dated June 30, 2026 says Assurance Assistant documentation was added for generating AI-powered responses to compliance and due diligence questions; the claim keeps the 'documentation' framing.
Decision guide sentence states Artifact provides on-demand access to compliance reports and Audit Manager automates evidence collection to assess whether controls operate effectively.

The quotes support that account agreements apply only to the signed-in account and that only the management account can accept organization agreements; that organization agreements apply to all accounts in the organization is only in the surrounding context, not in any quote.
FAQ sentence states Artifact Agreements is used to review, accept and track the status of AWS agreements such as the BAA.
Quotes state all AWS accounts have access to Artifact and that IAM users with non-admin permissions must be granted access using IAM permissions.
Quote under the BAA question heading states any AWS service may be used in a HIPAA Account but PHI may only be included in HIPAA Eligible Services; the BAA condition comes from the heading.
Quote states the Artifact NDA must be downloaded and agreed to before entering an agreement, and each agreement is confidential and cannot be shared outside the company.
Under the heading 'Is there a limit to the number of artifacts I can download?' the quote says all available artifacts can be downloaded at any time, as many times as needed.
Quote states Artifact Organization Agreements is only available for accounts using AWS Organizations.
Quote states Artifact Reports is used to download AWS security and compliance documents such as ISO certifications, PCI and SOC reports.
Quotes state reports may be shared with customers if permitted by the terms of the specific report, and customers can access reports with their own AWS account.
Quote describes creating IAM user credentials per auditor, limited to the reports relevant to that audit.
Quote states ISV compliance reports are only accessible to customers granted access to AWS Marketplace Vendor Insights for a specific ISV.
Quote states Artifact, available in the console, is a self-service audit artifact retrieval portal with on-demand access to compliance documentation and agreements.

Quotes state agreements can be reviewed, accepted and tracked for one account or multiple accounts in the organization, and with Organizations an agreement such as a BAA covers all existing and subsequent member accounts automatically.

Quotes state it is an AI-powered capability generating citation-backed responses about AWS services and security controls, available at no additional charge, with customer-side implementation out of scope.
Quotes state Artifact documents can be submitted to auditors or regulators to demonstrate AWS infrastructure compliance, and customers are responsible for documents about their own companies.
Quote states HIPAA-subject companies typically require a BAA, and in the Artifact console you review and accept such agreements and designate an account that can legally process PHI.
Quotes state downloading a report requires the required permissions and some reports require accepting Terms and conditions first.

Quote states email notifications for agreement and report updates are sent through AWS User Notifications, which needs notification hubs selected first; the commercial-Regions condition is in the page note.
Quote under Pricing states AWS provides Artifact documents and agreements free of charge.
Quote states Artifact also lets you download security and compliance documents for ISVs who sell on AWS Marketplace.
The quote supports on-demand downloads of ISO, PCI and SOC reports; 'certifications from accreditation bodies' is only in the next sentence of the context, not in the quote.
The quote supports terminating an agreement and activating it again; confirming acceptance and reviewing the terms are only in the preceding context sentence, not in the quote.

Quotes state each downloaded report is generated for you with a unique watermark, and confidential documents may be shared only within the company, with regulators and auditors, not with customers or on a website.
Doc-history row dated August 1, 2023 says the documentation for managing notifications was published.

The December 15, 2025 row records a documentation update (example policies, managed policy and download instructions) to accommodate the new ListReportVersions API; it does not state that AWS Artifact added the permission or API on that date, so the claim says more than the quote.
SRA quote states Artifact does not support delegated administration, access can be restricted to audit and compliance team IAM roles, and IAM policies can limit roles to specific reports.
Doc-history rows show third-party ISV reports launched in preview on November 30, 2022 and made generally available on January 27, 2023.
Table row: maximum accounts added or deleted per week for all aggregators is 1000, can be increased: Yes.
Table row: maximum number of accounts in an aggregator is 10000, can be increased: No.

The row and note support a limit of 50 aggregators that can be increased, with organization and account aggregators both counting; the 'per account' scope in the claim is not stated in the row, the note or the page intro (other rows on the page name 'per Region per account' explicitly; this one does not).
Doc-history row dated April 26, 2024 states CloudWatch metrics for monitoring Config data usage display only billable usage.
Rows under Single Account Conformance Packs: 50 conformance packs per account and 130 rules per conformance pack, both not increasable.
Decision guide quotes state Config gives a detailed view of resource configuration and lets you assess, audit and evaluate configurations for compliance with internal policies and regulations.
Quotes state EventBridge detects and reacts to changes in Config event status and invokes target actions when an event matches rule values.
FAQ quote states data aggregation cannot provision rules across accounts, is purely reporting, and StackSets can provision rules across accounts and Regions.
FAQ quote states data aggregation collects Config data from multiple accounts and Regions into a single account and a single Region.

Quote states an aggregator can be created in any account to aggregate compliance details from other accounts and from all accounts in an organization; the multi-Region part comes from the question heading.
Quote states accounts not in an AWS organization must each explicitly authorize the aggregator account.
